newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 10.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- The Supreme Public Prosecutors' Office decided on Monday to break up the student body Hanchongryon following last week's violence instigated by the organisation.
- Lee Han-dong, one of the aspirants for the presidential nomination ticket of the ruling New Korea Party, on Monday called for settlement of the 1992 campaign fund issue within this year.
- Lee Hoi-chang, chairman of the ruling New Korea Party, proposed that the President's power be decentralizsd to grant more strengh to the prime minister.
- South Korea asked Japan on Monday to stick to its "defense-only principle" in revising the 1978 U.S.-Japan defense guidelines.
- South Korea, the United States and Japan yesterday agreed that famine has begun gripping parts of North Korea and they will continue to provide humanitarian food aid to the North.
- Kia Motors, Hyundai and four other automakers on Monday called on Samsung to openly apologise for a report harmful to existing manufacturers.
- The first trial session for Kim Hyun-chul, President Kim Young-sam's second son, will begin June 23, a court official said. The junior Kim has been indicted on bribery and tax evasion charges.
